transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because work’s been… not going right. At the register I keep getting stuck doing odd things, like tapping the scanner a certain way or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting. Last week they wrote me up for it.

When you're doing those repetitive actions at work, like tapping the scanner, do you feel like you have to do them in a certain way to prevent something bad from happening, or do they feel more like an urge that you can't control?

It’s not really like I’m trying to stop something bad, no. It’s more… I just get stuck in it. Like the scanner tapping has a pattern, or my hand just stays over the drawer even though the customer’s right there. I know it doesn’t fit what’s happening, but I don’t move on fast enough.
Have you ever experienced sudden, brief movements or sounds that you couldn’t control, like blinking, shrugging, or making a noise?
Not really. I mean, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed anything like sudden noises or blinking I can’t control.

Have you ever had unwanted, intrusive thoughts that cause you distress, or found yourself doing mental acts—like counting or repeating words silently—to try to reduce that distress or prevent something bad from happening?
I don’t think so. I mean… I get stuck sometimes, but not because I’m counting in my head or trying to stop something from happening. Not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever had any uncontrollable movements or gestures, like sudden jerks, facial twitches, or unusual postures, that you couldn’t stop yourself from doing?

Not like jerks or twitches, no. It’s more that I get stuck doing something that doesn’t fit… like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just holding my hand over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting. I don’t really mean to. It got noticed at work last week.

When you get stuck doing these actions, like tapping the scanner or holding your hand still, do you feel a strong urge or discomfort before doing them, almost like you have to do them to feel 'just right' or to relieve some inner tension?

Not really like an urge, no. I don’t think I’m trying to make it feel “right.” I just… get stuck doing it. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern or holding my hand over the drawer while the person’s waiting. That’s the stuff that got me in trouble last week.
Do you ever feel a strong inner need or pressure to move in a certain way, like a feeling that builds up and you have to do the movement to release it?

No… I don’t really feel it building up like that. It’s more like I just get stuck doing something weird at the register—tapping the scanner in a pattern, or freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting. It got me written up last week.

When you find yourself stuck doing things like tapping the scanner or holding your hand still, are you fully aware of what you're doing at the time, or does it feel like you're spacing out or not completely in control of your thoughts?

I’m aware enough to know it looks wrong. I’m there at the register, and then I’m tapping the scanner in a pattern or just… stopped with my hand over the cash drawer while they’re waiting. It’s not like I plan it. It just happens, and last week they wrote me up for it.

Before you start tapping the scanner or holding your hand still, do you ever feel a strange sensation in your body or a need to do it that comes on suddenly, like an itch or pressure that you have to follow through with?

No, I don’t really notice an itch or pressure first. It’s more just… I’m at the register and I end up tapping the scanner, or I freeze with my hand over the drawer while the customer’s waiting. That’s what got me written up.

Before you start doing those things at the register—like tapping the scanner or freezing with your hand—do you ever feel a strange or uncomfortable sensation in your body that seems to lead into the action, even if you don’t feel like you have to do it to relieve it?

No… I haven’t noticed a body feeling before it. It’s more that I’m just at the register and I get stuck doing these things that don’t fit—like tapping the scanner a certain way, or my hand just staying over the cash drawer while someone’s waiting. That’s why I came in… it got me written up.
Do you ever feel a strange or uncomfortable sensation in your body just before you start tapping the scanner or holding your hand still, even if it doesn't feel like an urge to do the action?

I don’t think there’s a body feeling before it. It’s just… I’m at the register and I get stuck tapping the scanner or my hand freezes over the cash drawer while they’re waiting. That’s the part that got me written up.

Before you start doing those things at work—like tapping the scanner or holding your hand still—do you ever feel a sudden, strange feeling in your body that comes right before the action, even if it doesn’t make you feel like you have to do it?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed anything like that beforehand. It just kind of happens, as far as I can tell.

Do you ever feel a sudden urge or a need to move in a certain way just before you start tapping the scanner or holding your hand still, even if it doesn’t feel like something you have to do to make things right?

Not really an urge, no. I just… get stuck doing it at the register. Like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just stays over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. That’s what got me written up last week.
Do you ever notice any strange feelings in your body, like a tingling or pressure, just before you start tapping the scanner or holding your hand still at the register?

I haven’t really noticed tingling or pressure. It’s more just that I get stuck at the register—tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just kind of freezes over the cash drawer while the customer’s waiting. That’s what got me written up.
Do you ever notice any unusual sensations, like a tickle, tightness, or a feeling in your muscles, just before you start tapping the scanner or holding your hand still at the register?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed a tickle or tightness or anything in my muscles before it happens. It just sort of… happens.

Do you ever notice any unusual feelings in your body, like a tingling, tightness, or a pulling sensation, right before you start doing those things at the register, like tapping the scanner or holding your hand still?
I don’t think so. I mean… I haven’t noticed anything like that right before. It’s just hard to say.

Do you ever feel a strange or unusual sensation, like a tingling, pressure, or tightness, in any part of your body just before you start tapping the scanner or holding your hand still at the register?
Not that I can tell. I mean, I’ve tried to think about it, but I don’t notice tingling or tightness before it happens. It just… starts, I guess.
Have you ever had sudden, quick movements like blinking, facial twitches, or shoulder shrugs that you couldn’t control, even if they were brief?
I don’t think so. I mean, I blink like anyone, but not… sudden twitching or shoulder things that I can’t control, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you ever feel an inner restlessness or a need to move a certain part of your body, even if you don’t feel like you have to do it in a specific way or to make something right?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I feel restless like that… not in a way I’ve noticed, anyway.
